assertions.assertion: Reasoning is transition selection over explicit epistemic state; language is serialization.
The network proposes transitions and the VM decides legality.
Governance, physics, orchestration and an event ledger are modeled as distinct system concerns.
Independent pattern, heuristic and statistical guardians detect threats and report to a coordinating hub.
Agent execution is registry-gated, exact-capability bounded, fail-closed and evidence-producing.
Identity, policy, capability, deterministic planning, gated execution, audit and replay are independently testable stages.
Governed effects require policy evaluation, authority verification, proof and audit before effect.
Privacy/security capability claims remain acceptance-gated until end-to-end evidence exists.
Model output is advisory; host-owned capability policy and effect execution remain outside the model.
Authority, distributed mutation, permit lifecycle, execution and independent verification are separated and double-enforced.
Cycle, permit ledger, artifact order and authority ownership are modeled as separate invariant-bearing state machines.

The prior state store directly appended a second state lineage from observations and governance decisions; its hash-lineage mechanism is useful, but direct state advancement conflicts with CETA state-as-projection.
The prior audit ledger maintained a separate HMAC-protected hash chain over audit events; tamper-evidence is useful, but an independent audit chain cannot be canonical epistemic history.

The State Register event store used ordered append-only events, body hashes, prior/resulting roots, transactional writes, and chain verification; these are candidate mechanisms for one canonical transition ledger.
Builder audit uses canonicalized hash-linked events and verifies prior-hash continuity; this is retained as integrity/replay evidence, not as a second canonical state store.
Builder replay verifies audit-chain integrity rather than reconstructing epistemic state, so its replay contract is insufficient for CETA state reconstruction without rewrite.
TAAR appends per-run audit records with individual hashes but no cross-record previous-hash chain; the records remain useful fixtures but not canonical history.

The prior Builder apply path bounded workspace paths, staged rollback snapshots, rejected duplicate targets, and performed atomic file operations; these are adapter fixtures, while its direct apply API cannot remain a constitutional effect authority.

State Register actuators prepare and consume exact permits before effect and use separate optimizer/deployment verifier roles afterward; this supplies the strongest execution/verification separation mechanism in the corpus.

T.A.R.L. routes out-of-language side effects through one fail-closed mediation point before adapters act, including file, network, subprocess, FFI and tool calls; legality remains separate in the rebuild.
Direct rememberExplicit writes a new long-term memory node, while semantic embeddings and edges provide retrieval mechanics.
A universal node/edge graph can provide typed retrieval and provenance without proliferating independent memory tables.
An alternative action is acceptable only after it independently satisfies the same governance gate rather than inheriting the primary decision.
Evaluation, history, authority state/evidence/continuity, tests, verification and evaluation views are excluded from training material.
A specific failure cause may be assigned only when evidence supports it; otherwise the cause remains unresolved.
Weight changes require exact model, tokenizer, trainer, trusted checkpoint, resource bounds, evaluator, competence baseline and authorized transition path; hyperparameters may not be guessed.
Training and retrieval views are source-grounded while runtime state and held-out evaluation material remain separate.
